text:
priya: heads up — we had two edge nodes OOM yesterday due to a single customer opening lots of long-lived streams. symptoms: high KV memory + inflight buffers, OOM kill.

mike: can you paste the logs and rough counts?

priya: logs: `edge-03: mem 92% -> OOM kill` after ~380 concurrent streams from that org. each stream kept ~40k tokens worth of KV state. looks like unbounded inflight token window + client retries opening new streams without closing old ones.

elaine: is resume involved here or just long chats?

priya: different tenant, no resume. just long context chats + aggressive retry behavior.

jun: proposal: make the proxy enforce per-connection inflight accounting and expose two behaviors: hard reject at a hard_limit, and a soft "cold" lane where we spill oldest checkpoints to remote storage.

sam: prefer rejecting new connections (429) over silently dropping state. apps rely on determinism.

jun: sketch of config knobs:

```
edge.proxy.inflight_control:
  hard_limit_tokens: 20000
  soft_lane_threshold: 15000
  stream_idle_ttl_s: 120
  checkpoint_policy: async_spill_lru
```

mike: how do we count tokens? KV + queued/unacked + prefetch reserved? need consistent accounting.

priya: counting = len(KV) + queued_unacked + reserved_prefetch. infra implements hooks at allocation points.

elaine: soft lane behavior: accept stream but mark it cold and start async eviction; return a header so SDKs can surface degraded state.

sam: and for hard_limit, return 429 with Retry-After and a short resume token TTL so polite clients can reattach without replay.

elaine: example error body for 429:

```json
{
  "error": "inflight_limit_exceeded",
  "retry_after": 5,
  "resume_token_ttl": 30
}
```

jun: metrics/observability: edge.inflight.tokens, edge.streams.soft_lane, edge.checkpoint.evict, edge.oom.attributed_tenant should be emitted. add tracing spans to attribute memory spikes to tenant and soft_lane usage.

infra-bot: metric emitted: edge.inflight.tokens, edge.streams.soft_lane, edge.checkpoint.evict_count

mike: perf concern: checkpointing to redis will increase IO. consider batching evictions and writing to a local spill file before remote write for hot churn.

priya: agree. local spill + batched async flush to remote reduces peak IO. also throttle async flush if Redis slow.

sam: we should also cap prefetch on the server side: add `max_prefetch_tokens` per stream (default 2k), and require dedicated capacity for higher quotas.

devex: docs needed: SDK guidance for 429 handling, cold-lane hint, resume semantics, and backoff examples.

product: enterprise comms: tell customers about potential 429s during rollout and offer dedicated capacity to avoid these limits.

mike: rollout plan: feature flag `inflight_control_v2` default off. enable for 10% traffic, watch metrics, then expand. create alert when checkpoint.evict_count > 5x baseline.

priya: eng actions: implement allocation accounting, soft_lane plumbing, 429 payload. infra actions: feature flag + metrics + runbook.

jun: retry contract detail: on 429 we issue a short-lived resume token (30s). clients that get resume token can reconnect and resume without full replay. full resume for longer durations requires an explicit checkpoint.

sam: SDKs should implement exponential backoff + reuse resume token if present. I'll draft the SDK PR after the spec.

mike: I'll open the feature-flag ticket and alert runbook.

infra-bot: ticket created: EDGE-1427 (inflight-controls + soft-lane)

jun: timeline: tech spec by EOD tomorrow, pilot Wed, 10% Fri, full ramp conditional on no mem regressions next week.

priya: tagging @mike @jun for blockers. :thumbsup:
